anchors.trial: SOLVD-T + SOLVD-P (enalapril) via D2

source.citation: Kondo T, Jhund PS, McMurray JJV. Eur J Heart Fail 2022;24:421-430 (PMC9303189)

anchors.quote: SOLVD-T (Kondo Table 1): 'Enalapril (1285) ... 20 mg | 16.6 mg (E) 18.0 mg (P)'; SOLVD-P: '16.9 mg (E) e 18.2 mg (P) e'
anchors.arithmetic: D2: fraction 0.839 = (1285 x 16.6/20 + 2111 x 16.9/20) / (1285 + 2111) = (1066.6 + 1783.8)/3396 (SOLVD-T and SOLVD-P enalapril arms; protocol target 20 mg/day); x lowest flagged formulary target 20 mg/day = 16.79 mg/day.
anchors.notes: Lisinopril target is flagged at 20, 30 and 40 mg; the lowest (20) is the denominator as the engine's first-flagged target. No placebo-controlled lisinopril trial exists. ATLAS used 32.5-35 mg as the high arm.

anchors.trial: SOLVD-T + SOLVD-P

source.citation: Kondo T, Jhund PS, McMurray JJV. Eur J Heart Fail 2022;24:421-430 (PMC9303189)

anchors.quote: SOLVD-T (Kondo Table 1): 'Enalapril (1285) ... 20 mg | 16.6 mg (E) 18.0 mg (P)'; SOLVD-P: '16.9 mg (E) e 18.2 mg (P) e'
anchors.arithmetic: D1: patient-weighted mean of enalapril-arm means = (1285 x 16.6 + 2111 x 16.9)/3396 = 16.79 mg/day; fraction 16.79/20 = 0.839.
anchors.notes: DENOMINATOR CAVEAT: 16.6 and 16.9 are doses among patients still on drug at the last visit. In SOLVD-T 32.5% of the enalapril group had discontinued; 16.6 x (1 - 0.325) = 11.2 mg, the all-randomized mean the same footnote reports, and Lam 2018 says 'final mean daily dose of either study drug was 11 mg'. The trial RR is an intention-to-treat estimate, so it reflects the diluted 11.2 mg average exposure; the on-drug dose is 16.6. Judgement: anchor kept at the on-drug dose (a patient modelled as taking the drug), flagged for the controller. SAVE, AIRE and TRACE patients (73% of the pooled 12,763) have no verified dose.

source.citation: Kondo T, Jhund PS, McMurray JJV. Eur J Heart Fail 2022;24:421-430 (PMC9303189)

anchors.quote: COPERNICUS | Carvedilol (1156) Placebo (1133) | ... | 50 mg | 37 mg (C) e 41 mg (P) e | 65% (C) e 78% (P) e

source.citation: Kondo T, Jhund PS, McMurray JJV. Eur J Heart Fail 2022;24:421-430 (PMC9303189)

anchors.quote: CIBIS II | Bisoprolol (1327) Placebo (1320) | ... | 10 mg | 6.2 mg (B) 7.3 mg (P) (Kondo)  versus Tillman: 'CIBIS-II 10 Bisoprolol (8.6 mg daily) versus placebo'
anchors.arithmetic: D3 -> D2: fraction 0.775 = (1990 x 159/200 + 1156 x 37/50)/(1990+1156) = (1582.05 + 855.44)/3146; x 10 mg = 7.75 mg/day. Both CIBIS-II figures recorded: 6.2 mg (0.62) and 8.6 mg (0.86); the proxy sits between them.
anchors.notes: CIBIS-II is excluded from the pooled fraction because its mean cannot be settled from a primary source. Tillman's CIBIS-II row also says 'No significant difference in all-cause death', which contradicts the trial abstract (HR 0.66, p<0.0001), so that row is unreliable. Distribution facts read from a review citing the Lancet paper: 564 (42.5%) on 10 mg, 152 on 7.5, 176 on 5 in the maintenance phase; Simon 2003: 434 on 1.25-3.75 mg. Computed from those counts, the mean of the 892 patients on 5 mg or more is 8.59 mg (matches 8.6), and the mean of all 1,327 would be 6.2-7.0 mg depending on the low-dose split (matches the low end near 6.2). So 8.6 may be a mean among patients on 5 mg or more and 6.2 a mean that counts the low-dose group, but this is inference, not a settled fact.

low_dose_credit.notes: Doses are end-of-titration means (Kondo Table 4); whole-trial means were 3.2 and 22.5 mg (ratio 0.142; nominal midpoints 3.75/33.75 = 0.111). Low dose = 4.5/2.5 = 1.8 times the lisinopril label start. Engine today at 4.5 mg: 0.6 + 0.4 x (4.5-2.5)/(20-2.5) = 0.646. The HR CI crosses 1, so the credit for death is essentially unbounded (0.11 to 1.13). RR(high) is a class value measured at about 17 mg enalapril, not at 33 mg lisinopril.

low_dose_credit.arithmetic: HR not reported. HF hospitalizations (events): high 1,199 vs low 1,576, ratio 0.761 (computed; the abstract says '24% fewer hospitalizations for heart failure (P=0.002)'). RR(low) = 0.67/0.761 = 0.8807; credit = ln(0.8807)/ln(0.67) = -0.1271/-0.4005 = 0.317.
low_dose_credit.notes: Counts are hospitalization EVENTS from a secondary review of the Circulation paper (Cardiology Trials), not patients, and no HR/CI was found in any fetched source, so 0.761 is an approximation. The HFH row RR 0.67 is a Peto odds ratio of patients readmitted.

Nominal 50/150 mg = 0.333. Low arm 46 mg = 1.84 times the losartan label start of 25 mg. Engine today at 46 mg: 0.6 + 0.4 x (46-25)/(150-25) = 0.667. Credit is unstable: HR CI includes 1 and RR(high) CI reaches 0.98. HEAAL patients were ACE inhibitor intolerant; the RR(high) row is CHARM candesartan (0.88).
450 vs 503 patients admitted for HF (abstract). The credit runs from 0.00 to 0.93 across the HR interval.
